assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

A tool call that a permission POLICY auto-allows, instead of asking. On 2.x the policy is the per-cell `permission` config: `bash: allow` covers the shell tool (the record's probe, measured: a project-local `bash: allow` ran a `date` shell call with no ask, while the sandbox's global `bash: ask` raised one). With the call allowed, no `permission.asked` reaches the daemon, so the session never enters waiting; it stays working through the call and ends ready.
caveats: The negative is the point: the session must NOT show waiting, because the policy decided — an ask under the global `bash: ask` would.

sources.note: 2.x hook receiver: permission.asked holds waiting, session.execution.{succeeded,failed,interrupted} end the turn through HandleStopHook (#2108)
each assistant row's model.id is the step's ModelName; text items feed applyAssistantText (task-estimate scan)

preconditions: One OpenCode 2.x `serve --service` running, with a model it can reach (this host: the sandbox service, local Kolibri-1 4-bit model (mlx_lm) at 127.0.0.1:8087); the rig never starts, stops or reconfigures it
The three XDG exports, coexist IRRLICHT_ONBOARD_HOME and a non-7837 bind address from replaydata/agents/opencode-v2/prerequisites.md; OPENCODE_DB unset
setup: driver-interactive.sh (API driver) refuses before creating anything unless exactly one `serve --service` runs, its environment carries the run's XDG_* values, and the plugin's beacon resolves this run's daemon

It creates one session over POST /api/session at <staging>/cwd, waits for the service log to show the plugin the daemon installed loading for that location with no load failure, then drives the script; the session's session_message rows are exported read-only as the transcript
settings allow the shell tool (`permission.bash: allow`) in RUN_CWD/opencode.json; the sandbox's global config asks for it

script.text: Run the shell command `echo hello` using your shell tool. Then reply with exactly: done

verify: working through the auto-allowed shell call, never waiting
